title: First 72 Hours Post-Go-Live: Stability, Observability, and Cost-Control Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes the operational runbook for the first 72 hours after an enterprise customer goes live on Redwood (hosted, dedicated, or private). The goal is to stabilize traffic, validate cost controls, confirm quality metrics, and provide clear escalation paths if production behavior diverges from expectations. Use this document as the canonical checklist for Customer Success (CS), Oncall, and Platform Engineers during the initial post-cutover period.

Scope and objectives
--------------------
- Scope: Applies to enterprise cutovers where a customer begins production traffic to Redwood inference endpoints for the first time or after major migration. Includes hosted API, Dedicated tenants, and Private deployments.
- Objectives (first 72h):
  - Ensure customer-facing SLOs are met (latency, availability).
  - Validate cost/usage profile against the agreed ramp plan and trigger throttles or quota protections if anomalies occur.
  - Confirm model fidelity (no major quality regressions vs. eval baselines).
  - Maintain clear communications to customer stakeholders and internal execs.

Owner and primary contacts
--------------------------
- Playbook owner: Customer Success (Maya Chen)
- Oncall escalation: Platform Oncall (rotation lead) — contact via #oncall-pager Slack and PagerDuty escalation: ENG-PLATFORM-PG
- Customer-facing lead: assigned CSM and Solutions Engineer (listed in cutover runbook)
- Exec escalation: Head of Customer Success (Priya Singh)

Pre-cutover checklist (completed during go/no-go window)
-------------------------------------------------------
1) Configuration validation (CS / Solutions Eng)
   - Confirm API key provisioning and tenant mapping.
   - Validate routing and VPC peering / private network rules.
   - Confirm dedicated capacity reservation and autoscale limits for Dedicated customers.
2) Telemetry and observability
   - Ensure synthetic probes are configured for: latency P50/P95, error rate, token-per-request distribution, and model-quality sentinel prompts.
   - Verify metrics forwarding and access for customer telemetry (Prometheus, OTLP, or partner CTX).
3) Cost guardrails
   - Set conservative quota/ratelimits for first 24h: initial quota = 30% of expected ramp unless customer requests otherwise.
   - Configure quota-protector webhook with emergency override and alerting to CS.
4) Communication plan
   - Publish cutover schedule and primary contacts to customer and internal stakeholders.
   - Pre-stage status page entries and templated customer messages.

Immediate post-cutover (0–4 hours) — stabilization window
-------------------------------------------------------
Action items (who / what / timeframe):
- 0–15 minutes: confirm API key acceptance and successful token exchange with 3 probe requests across customer regions. (Solutions Eng)
- 15–60 minutes: verify streaming and synchronous endpoints respond under expected concurrency. Check P50/P95 latency against target. (Platform Oncall)
- 30–90 minutes: ensure KV cache hit-rate (if configured) is within expected range; validate cold-start behavior and warmup logs. (Runtime team)
- 60–120 minutes: validate billing meter increments and initial usage appears in cost dashboards. (Finance Ops + CS)
- 120–240 minutes: review model-quality sentinel runs and manual spot-check 10-20 samples for hallucination/regression. (CS + Applied ML)

First 24 hours — defensive posture and telemetry escalation
--------------------------------------------------------
- Maintain conservative quotas and allow scheduled step-ups only after stability is proven for 4 consecutive 15-minute windows.
- Key dashboards to watch (links or names):
  - Tenant health overview: availability, total requests, token throughput
  - Runtime performance: GPU utilization, batching latency, KV cache metrics
  - Cost telemetry: tokens/sec, cost-per-token estimate, billing-meter lag
  - Model-quality sentinel: BLEU/ROUGE proxy metrics and classification/regression diffs
- Automated alerts to treat as P0 during first 24h:
  - Availability < 99% in a 5-minute window
  - Error rate > 2% sustained for 10 minutes
  - Token cost spike > 40% over expected baseline (10m moving avg)
  - Sudden drop in model-quality sentinel score > 15% from baseline
- Communications cadence: hourly status updates to customer by CSM for first 8 hours, then every 4 hours until 24h if stable.

24–72 hours — measured ramp and post-cutover validation
-----------------------------------------------------
- If the first 24 hours are stable, gradually increase quotas to planned ramp over the next 48 hours in pre-agreed increments (example: 30% -> 60% -> 100%). Only increase when the following are green for 30 minutes: latency P95, error rate, cost delta.
- Run a structured quality regression check at 48 hours using the agreed eval prompt set (report outputs to both CS and Applied ML).
- Conduct a billing reconciliation snapshot at 48 hours (Finance Ops) and confirm customers are seeing expected metering.

Rollback and emergency mitigations
---------------------------------
- Immediate rollback (trigger conditions): severe latency regression (P95 > 2x SLO for 30m), catastrophic error rate (>10%), or critical data-exposure alert.
- Rollback steps (Platform Oncall):
  1) Switch routing to the previous stable model/variant via traffic-split control (documented in deployment runbook).
  2) If tenant-level, trigger tenant quiesce and move to safe-fallback pool.
  3) Notify CSM and CS leadership; open incident in status tool and declare severity.
  4) If routing cannot be switched, throttle at the API gateway and enable degraded-mode responses with client-friendly error messages.
- Post-rollback postmortem: Rapid RCA within 24h (comprised of Platform, Runtime, Applied ML, CS). Follow with full P1 postmortem within 72h.

Escalation matrix and contact templates
--------------------------------------
- P0: Platform Oncall -> Platform Eng Lead -> Head of Platform -> CTO (pager escalation).
- P1: CS Lead -> Solutions Eng -> Platform Oncall.
- For each escalation, use templated messages: initial incident summary, impact to customer, mitigation steps in progress, ETA for next update.
- Example customer update (30m after detection):
  "Hello <CustomerContacts>, we detected elevated error rates affecting your inference traffic. Our oncall team has scoped the issue and is performing a controlled rollback to the previous model variant. We will follow up within 30 minutes with progress and impact details. We apologize for the disruption and are prioritizing restoration of service."

Operational controls and automation recipes
-----------------------------------------
- Auto-throttle policy: enable adaptive rate limiter for first 24h with action types: 429 throttle -> 503 degrade -> webhook to CS for manual override.
- Canary synthetic schedule: 1 probe every minute from three global vantage points, escalate after 3 consecutive failures.
- Quota protector: require two-step approval for quota increases >25% during first 72h. Approvals logged to audit trail.

Monitoring thresholds (recommended defaults)
-----------------------------------------
| Metric | Warning threshold | Critical threshold | Owner |
|--------|-------------------|--------------------|-------|
| Availability (tenant) | < 99.5% (5m) | < 99% (5m) | Platform Oncall |
| Error rate | > 1% (10m) | > 2% (10m) | Platform Oncall |
| P95 latency | > 1.5x SLO | > 2x SLO | Runtime Team |
| Token cost delta | > 20% | > 40% | Finance Ops |
| Model-quality sentinel | drop > 10% | drop > 15% | Applied ML |

Note: thresholds above should be calibrated to the customer's SLOs and contract.

Customer communications and status templates
------------------------------------------
- Pre-approved short-form status updates, incident acknowledgement, and recovery confirmation templates are stored in the shared CS templates library. Use the following minimum fields in every update: timestamp, impact (users/requests affected), mitigation steps, ETA, contact person, and link to incident page.

Post-72h wrap-up and QBR inputs
-------------------------------
- 72-hour deliverables:
  - Stability sign-off from Platform Oncall and CS (signed checklist).
  - Cost variance report vs. expected ramp with explanations for deltas.
  - Model-quality regression report and any corrective actions taken.
  - Customer debrief meeting scheduled within 5 business days; include QBR artifacts if onboarding impacted contractual metrics.
- Suggested QBR artifacts: time-series of tokens, cost per token, P50/P95 latency, error rate, sentinel evaluation scores, and a list of action items and owners.

Appendix A — Useful commands and snippets
----------------------------------------
- Check tenant routing: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/tenants/<TENANT_ID>/routing/status
- Force a traffic-split rollback (CLI example): redwoodctl route update --tenant <TENANT_ID> --from <NEW_VARIANT> --to <OLD_VARIANT> --force --reason "post-go-live rollback"
- Quota protector webhook payload (example):
  {
    "tenant_id": "<TENANT_ID>",
    "requested_increase_pct": 50,
    "requested_by": "csm@example.com"
  }
